definitions.definition: Torus=reals/(2*pi*integers), with normalized measure dx/(2*pi). Periodic spatial products, integrals and derivatives are on this torus. A trigonometric polynomial is a finite sum of exp(i*k*x) with integer k.

For a periodic integrable f, hat f(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x)exp(-i*k*x) dx, k in Z. Extend Fourier coefficients to periodic distributions. Reality means hat f(-k)=conjugate(hat f(k)); mean zero means hat f(0)=0. For sequences, ell^2 is the square-summable sequence space with counting measure.

For nonzero integers a,b,c,d with a+b+c+d=0, let N1>=N2>=N3>=N4 be the decreasing rearrangement of |a|,|b|,|c|,|d|, resolving ties in any order. Nthird(a,b,c,d)=N3. Thus N3 is the second smallest of all four magnitudes including the dual output.

output.statement: There is an absolute C such that for all nonnegative x1,x2,x3,x4 in ell^2(Z\{0}), sum_{a+b+c+d=0,abcd!=0} x1(a)x2(b)x3(c)x4(d)/Nthird(a,b,c,d)<=C*product_{j=1}^4||xj||_(ell^2). The sum is the supremum of finite positive partial sums; the same bound holds when it is restricted to any subset of quadruples.

argument.text: Fix four sequences x1,x2,x3,x4 and assume L1: they are nonnegative and in ell^2(Z\{0}). First truncate to finite support. Partition the nonzero integers into shells 2^j<=|k|<2^(j+1), j>=0, and let Xshell_(r,j) be the corresponding ell^2 norm. Sum over the at most 24 orderings of the four shell indices; relabel the sequence positions within one ordering so j1>=j2>=j3>=j4. The zero-sum relation implies the largest frequency <=3 times the second largest, hence j1-j2<=2. For each fixed pair of frequencies in the smaller shells, the sum over the remaining two with prescribed sum is at most the product of their ell^2 norms by Cauchy-Schwarz (a translated reflection preserves the norm). Each smaller shell has <=2^(j+1) integers. Taking their ell^1 norms by Cauchy-Schwarz gives a shell contribution <=C*2^((j3+j4)/2)*product_r Xshell_(r,jr). Dividing by Nthird>=2^j3 leaves C*2^(-(j3-j4)/2)*product_r Xshell_(r,jr).

produces.statement: For every ordered interacting nonnegative shell tuple s1>=s2>=s3>=s4, 0<=s1-s2<=2 and its weighted four-linear contribution is <=C*2^(-(s3-s4)/2)*Xshell_(1,s1)*Xshell_(2,s2)*Xshell_(3,s3)*Xshell_(4,s4).

argument.text: For q=j1-j2 in {0,1,2}, drop the upper restrictions on the smaller shell indices in this nonnegative sum. The resulting bound factors as C*(sum_J Xshell_(1,J)Xshell_(2,J-q))*(sum_(ell>=m>=0)2^(-(ell-m)/2)Xshell_(3,ell)Xshell_(4,m)). The first factor is <=||Xshell_1||_ell2||Xshell_2||_ell2. In the second, write r=ell-m and apply Cauchy-Schwarz for each r; it is <=sum_(r>=0)2^(-r/2)||Xshell_3||_ell2||Xshell_4||_ell2=||Xshell_3||_ell2||Xshell_4||_ell2/(1-2^(-1/2)). Shell orthogonality gives ||Xshell_r||_ell2=||x_r||_ell2. Summing the 24 orderings and three offsets proves the finite-support inequality with an absolute constant.

produces.statement: There is an absolute C such that for every finite-support nonnegative ell^2 quadruple y1,y2,y3,y4, sum_(a+b+c+d=0,abcd!=0)y1(a)y2(b)y3(c)y4(d)/Nthird(a,b,c,d)<=C*product_(j=1)^4||yj||_ell2.

argument.text: For general inputs apply F002 to x_r restricted to |k|<=m and let m tend to infinity. Each norm is bounded by the full ell^2 norm. Every finite set of contributing quadruples is included at some m, and the nonnegative infinite sum is defined as the supremum of those finite sums. Therefore the same bound holds without exchanging conditionally convergent series. Restricting to any subset decreases a nonnegative sum. Discharge L1 and quantify the four inputs; this proves the asserted conclusion.
